fullPassage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 명확한 방식으로 정보를 제공함으로써 '매출 증가의 가능성(increasing sales)'이 올라간다
det.analysis:
✅ ① increasing sales: 매출 증가 → 'the possibility of increasing sales goes up'이 원문 일치. 명확한 정보 제공의 결과 ←정답
❌ ② reducing costs: 비용 절감 → 본문에서 비용에 대한 언급 없음
❌ ③ losing customers: 고객 상실 → 매출을 높이려는 맥락과 반대
❌ ④ changing regulations: 규정 변경 → 본문에서 규정에 대한 언급 없음
det.tip: By doing so = 명확하고 정직한 방식으로 정보를 제공함으로써 → 매출 증가 가능성 상승

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 상품이나 서비스를 소비자에게 그 '가치(value)'가 명확하게 드러나는 방식으로 홍보한다
det.analysis:
❌ ① price: 가격 → 본문은 상품의 가격이 아닌 가치를 강조
❌ ② brand: 브랜드 → 브랜드 명확성이 아닌 상품의 가치가 맥락의 핵심
❌ ③ origin: 출처 → 본문에서 출처에 대한 언급 없음
✅ ④ value: 가치 → 'makes the value clear to the consumer'가 원문 일치. 상품의 가치를 소비자에게 명확히 한다는 맥락 ←정답
det.tip: makes the value clear = 가치를 명확히 한다. 정직한 마케팅의 핵심 전략

questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. ①<u>Gone</u> are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers ②<u>fooled</u> once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to ③<u>promoting</u> that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how ④<u>to reach</u> them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ promoting → promote. to부정사 병렬 구조: to identify ... and to promote
det.analysis:
❌ ① Gone: 도치 구문 'Gone are the days ~'는 정상 어법. 보어(Gone)가 문두에 나온 주격보어 도치
❌ ② fooled: 과거분사 후치수식. consumers (who were) fooled once = 한번 속은 소비자. 정상
✅ ③ promoting: 오류. 앞의 'to identify ... and to ___'에서 to부정사 병렬이므로 promote(동사 원형)가 되어야 함. promoting은 동명사/현재분사로 병렬 불일치 ←정답
❌ ④ to reach: 'how to reach them'은 의문사+to부정사 구문으로 정상
det.tip: to identify ... and to promote → 병렬 구조는 같은 형태 유지

questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really ②<u>want</u> or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers ③<u>whose</u> are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know ④<u>where</u> the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ whose → who. 관계대명사 주격: the consumers who are most likely to appreciate
det.analysis:
❌ ① force: 'force + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문으로 정상. force people to think
❌ ② want: 'something they did not really want or need'에서 관계대명사(목적격) 생략 + 동사 원형 want/need 병렬. 정상
✅ ③ whose: 오류. 'the consumers who are most likely ~'에서 주격 관계대명사 who가 필요. whose는 소유격 관계대명사이므로 뒤에 명사가 와야 하는데 are(동사)가 바로 옴 ←정답
❌ ④ where: 간접의문문 'know where the potential consumers are'에서 장소를 묻는 의문부사 where 사용 정상
det.tip: who vs whose: who + 동사 (주격) / whose + 명사 (소유격)

The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate ③<u>their</u> experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way ④<u>what</u> makes the value clear to the consumer. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ what → that. 선행사 a way를 수식하는 관계대명사 that이 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① is used: 수동태 'promotion is used to provide'로 정상. 주어 promotion이 사용되는 것이므로 수동태 적절
❌ ② purchasing: 'fool A into -ing' 구문으로 정상. into 뒤에 동명사 purchasing 적절
❌ ③ their: 'consumers fooled once'를 선행사로 하는 소유격 대명사 their 사용 정상. 자신의 경험을 전달
✅ ④ what: 오류. 'in a way that makes the value clear'에서 선행사 a way가 있으므로 관계대명사 that이 필요. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 a way와 함께 쓸 수 없음 ←정답
det.tip: 선행사 있으면 that/which, 선행사 없으면 what. a way + that(관계대명사)

questions.passage: ①We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear fashion possible. ②By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. ③Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchased something. ④The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good.

det.korean: ③번 purchased → purchasing. 'fool A into -ing' 구문에서 동명사가 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①②③: ③은 오류 문장 (purchased → purchasing)
✅ ② ①②④: ①②④는 모두 어법상 올바름. ③만 오류 ←정답
❌ ③ ①③④: ③은 오류 문장
❌ ④ ②③④: ③은 오류 문장
det.tip: fool A into -ing: '~를 속여 ~하게 하다'. into 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)만 가능
